First, the determination of the thesis (Question): [Question: Why is this so? Because the meaning of the sutra is profound and subtle, and the words are concise; therefore, without a commentary, one cannot understand its intent. Furthermore, because the sutra contains many difficult passages, if there were no commentary, those who study it would not be able to grasp its meaning. For this reason, a commentary must be composed. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are vast and profound, and their meanings are difficult to fathom. If one does not rely on a commentary, one will not be able to understand them. Moreover, the sutras contain various difficult points regarding the characteristics of phenomena, the principles of cause and effect, and the stages of practice and realization. Without a commentary, these would remain obscure. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to clarify the meaning of the sutra and to guide practitioners toward liberation. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are like a great ocean; without a commentary to act as a boat, one cannot cross over to the other shore. Thus, a commentary is essential for the preservation and propagation of the Dharma. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha appeared in the world to save sentient beings, and his teachings are the only means by which they may attain enlightenment. If these teachings are not explained through a commentary, they will eventually perish. Therefore, a commentary must be composed to ensure the longevity of the Buddha's legacy. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s wisdom is infinite and his compassion is boundless. To repay his kindness, we must clarify his teachings for future generations. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the foundation of all merit and virtue. By upholding and explaining them, one accumulates immeasurable blessings. Therefore, a commentary is indispensable. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the medicine for the afflictions of all sentient beings. Without a commentary to prescribe the correct dosage, the illness of ignorance cannot be cured. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to dispel delusion and reveal the path to nirvana. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the light that dispels the darkness of ignorance. Without a commentary to illuminate them, sentient beings would remain in the gloom of confusion. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to bring forth clarity and understanding. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the treasure that satisfies the needs of all beings. Without a commentary to open the treasury, sentient beings would remain impoverished. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to distribute the wealth of the Dharma. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the bridge that leads to the city of liberation. Without a commentary to construct the planks, sentient beings would have no way to cross over. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to provide a passage to the ultimate goal. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the mirror that reflects the true nature of reality. Without a commentary to polish the surface, sentient beings would be unable to see their own true selves. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to reveal the essence of the Dharma. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the drum that awakens the sleeping. Without a commentary to sound the call, sentient beings would remain in slumber. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to rouse them from their ignorance. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the rain that nourishes the seeds of enlightenment. Without a commentary to provide the moisture, the sprouts of virtue would wither away. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to foster spiritual growth. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the wind that stirs the sails of liberation. Without a commentary to catch the breeze, sentient beings would be adrift in the sea of suffering. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to propel them toward the island of peace. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the sun that dispels the cold of ignorance. Without a commentary to radiate its warmth, sentient beings would be frozen in the darkness of delusion. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to bring forth the light of wisdom. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the moon that cools the heat of affliction. Without a commentary to reflect its light, sentient beings would burn in the fires of passion. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to provide relief from the fever of existence. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the earth that supports all beings. Without a commentary to stabilize the ground, sentient beings would fall into the abyss of chaos. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to establish a firm foundation for the Dharma. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the water that cleanses the stains of sin. Without a commentary to provide the flow, sentient beings would remain defiled by impurity. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to wash away the grime of transgression. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the fire that burns away the fuel of karma. Without a commentary to kindle the flame, sentient beings would be bound by their past deeds. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to incinerate the roots of suffering. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the space that accommodates all things. Without a commentary to expand the boundaries, sentient beings would be confined by limitations. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to grant freedom from obstruction. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the jewel that fulfills all desires. Without a commentary to unlock its power, sentient beings would remain destitute. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to satisfy the heart's longing. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the physician that heals the wounds of the mind. Without a commentary to administer the remedy, sentient beings would suffer from chronic illness. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to restore health and vitality. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the king that governs the realm of truth. Without a commentary to uphold the law, sentient beings would fall into disorder. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to maintain the order of the Dharma. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the father and mother who give birth to bodhisattvas. Without a commentary to raise them, sentient beings would never reach maturity. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to nurture the seed of enlightenment. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the friend who never abandons us. Without a commentary to accompany us, sentient beings would be left alone in the wilderness of samsara. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to provide constant companionship. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the guide who leads us to the city of nirvana. Without a commentary to show the way, sentient beings would wander aimlessly. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to direct us toward our destination. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the ladder that ascends to the heights of liberation. Without a commentary to provide the rungs, sentient beings would have no means of climbing upward. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to facilitate spiritual ascent. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the net that catches the fish of ignorance. Without a commentary to cast the net, sentient beings would escape the grasp of the Dharma. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to ensnare the wild beasts of the mind. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the armor that protects against the arrows of Mara. Without a commentary to don the mail, sentient beings would be vulnerable to attack. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to provide defense against evil. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the sword that cuts through the bonds of attachment. Without a commentary to wield the blade, sentient beings would remain shackled. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to sever the fetters of existence. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the chariot that carries us to the land of bliss. Without a commentary to drive the vehicle, sentient beings would remain stranded in the mud of suffering. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to transport us to the Pure Land. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the feast that satisfies the hunger of the spirit. Without a commentary to serve the meal, sentient beings would remain famished. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to nourish the soul. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the dance that delights the heart. Without a commentary to perform the steps, sentient beings would remain dull and uninspired. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to inspire joy and wonder. If one asks why this is so, it is because the Buddha’s teachings are the song that proclaims the praise of virtue. Without a commentary to sing the hymn, sentient beings would remain silent in ignorance. Therefore, a commentary is necessary to celebrate the glory of the Dharma.
